name: Real-time power scheduling
definition: Scheduling and correcting real-time power trades, imports and positions with the CAISO and counterparties, and staffing the real-time schedule.

synthesis.description: The real-time desk lead sends the shift traders a steady stream of instructions and position updates: open longs and shorts by hub and hour, purchases and sales to enter in Enpower under named books, deal numbers to use for transmission, checkout calls with marketers and utilities each night, and the monthly shift schedule. Traders keep preschedule and EPE schedule sheets, submit schedules and tags to the CISO, and correct mistakes found afterwards, such as wrong import IDs, duplicate schedules, wrong lending amounts or schedules misentered by the CISO.
steps: The desk lead or preschedulers report the day's positions and deals by hub and hour.
Shift traders enter purchases and sales in Enpower under the right books and deal numbers.
Schedules and tags are submitted to the CISO and counterparties, with hourly calls where required.
Traders check out with major marketers and utilities each night.
Errors in the schedule sheets, tags or CISO entries are found and corrected.
Shift coverage and rule changes are circulated to the group.
stalls: Schedule sheets repeatedly carry errors that have to be reworked: duplicate schedules, wrong lending positions and missing schedules in the EPE sheet.
Wrong import IDs and schedules misentered at the CISO force corrections after submission.
Systems fail during the shift: the CISO cannot read submitted bids, trading screens stop working and Enpower is taken down for maintenance.
When deals are not recorded during a shift, traders on that shift have to reconstruct the sheet afterwards.
A requested task was put off to another day for lack of time.
contradictions: The EPE schedule sheets disagree with the actual lending deals: the sheet showed a lending position the desk had to correct, and later the lending in the EPE schedules was recorded at a different volume from the deal with PSCO.
A trader's spreadsheet showed a dispatch figure that the desk lead questioned against what was actually scheduled.
synthesis.approach: Generate the preschedule and EPE schedule sheets from the deals booked in Enpower, with checks that flag duplicate schedules, lending volumes that differ from the deal, and import IDs or tags that do not match the CISO submission. A nightly checkout report listing positions by counterparty and hour would replace manual reconciliation, and a written shift procedure would hold the standing rules now repeated by email.
synthesis.rationale: Much of the email restates standing rules (hourly calls, deal numbers for transmission, nightly checkout, where to book real-time purchases) and corrects sheet errors. A desk procedure gives every shift the same rules, and the generated sheets with checks attack the rework that recurs most.

estimate.label: estimate, not a count
estimate.rationale: A round usually means entering or adjusting deals in Enpower, updating the preschedule or EPE sheet, and checking positions or tags against the CISO and counterparties; correction rounds add finding and fixing a wrong import ID, lending volume or duplicate schedule, and occasionally reconstructing a shift's sheet. Simple position notices take little; reconstruction drives the high end. Sheet building and mismatch checks are the automatable part.
